\chapter{Tickets, Seats and Trouble}
\label{ch:ka-tickets-seats-and-trouble}
\hlchaptermodality{314}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can buy a ticket and a seat, ask when the bus or train leaves, say I have missed the bus or lost my bag and report it, ask for medicine, and read the letter \kn{ಔ} in auṣadha.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 314: buy a ticket, ask the time, report a problem on a trip, and read and write \kn{ಔ}.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸೀಟು} (sīṭu)}{ಸೀಟು (sīṭu)}]{\kn{ಸೀಟು} (sīṭu) — a seat}

\label{lesson:KA-C314-situ}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}a ticket\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}a bus\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}a train\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{ṭikeṭ}, \emph{bas}, \emph{railu}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}Go straight on.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{nēravāgi hōgi}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸೀಟು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸೀಟು}} — \emph{sīṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}a seat (on a bus or a train)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಈ} \kn{ಸೀಟು} \kn{ಖಾಲಿ} \kn{ಇದೆಯಾ}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ī sīṭu khāli ideyā?} — \textquotedblleft{}Is this seat free?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಖಾಲಿ}}, \textquotedblleft{}empty\textquotedblright{}, says the seat is free. \textbf{\kn{ಇದೆಯಾ}} is \textbf{\kn{ಇದೆ}} with the question ending \textbf{-\kn{ಆ}}, the one in \textbf{\kn{ನಿಮಗೆ} \kn{ಕಾಫಿ} \kn{ಇಷ್ಟವಾ}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಕಿಟಕಿಯ} \kn{ಪಕ್ಕದ} \kn{ಸೀಟು} \kn{ಬೇಕು}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanage kiṭakiya pakkada sīṭu bēku.} — \textquotedblleft{}I would like a seat by the window.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಕಿಟಕಿಯ} \kn{ಪಕ್ಕದ}} (\emph{kiṭakiya pakkada}, \textquotedblleft{}by the window\textquotedblright{}): \textquotedblleft{}of the window's side\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸೀಟು}} (\emph{sīṭu}) is English \emph{seat}, borrowed with a final \textbf{-\kn{ಉ}}, as \textbf{\kn{ಸ್ಕೇಲು}} is English \emph{scale}. Others keep their last consonant bare, as \textbf{\kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್}} and \textbf{\kn{ಬಸ್}} do. Both habits live side by side in Kannada.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{sīṭu}, slowly, then at speed
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Is this seat free?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ī sīṭu khāli ideyā?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I would like a seat by the window\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nanage kiṭakiya pakkada sīṭu bēku}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\kn{ಸೀಟು}} mean? (\textbf{A seat}, on a bus or a train.) \textquotedblleft{}Is this seat free?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\kn{ಈ} \kn{ಸೀಟು} \kn{ಖಾಲಿ} \kn{ಇದೆಯಾ}?}) Where does the word come from? (\textbf{English \emph{seat}.})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ} (ondu ṭikeṭ koḍi)}{ಒಂದು ಟಿಕೆಟ್ ಕೊಡಿ (ondu ṭikeṭ koḍi)}]{\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ} (ondu ṭikeṭ koḍi) — at the ticket window}

\label{lesson:KA-C314-tiket-kodi}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a seat\textquotedblright{} (\emph{sīṭu}) and \textquotedblleft{}Is this seat free?\textquotedblright{} (\emph{ī sīṭu khāli ideyā?}). Then \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{koḍu}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: buying a ticket}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ} \kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maisūrige ondu ṭikeṭ koḍi.} — \textquotedblleft{}One ticket to Mysuru, please.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಕೊಡಿ}} is the polite \textquotedblleft{}give\textquotedblright{}, like the \textbf{\kn{ಹೋಗಿ}} of directions. The place takes \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\kn{ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ}}, as \textbf{\kn{ಊರಿಗೆ}}. For two people: \textbf{\kn{ಎರಡು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṣṭu āyitu?} — \textquotedblleft{}How much is it?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}how much has it come to?\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\kn{ಆಯಿತು}} of \textquotedblleft{}it happened, it became\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ನಾಳೆಯ} \kn{ರೈಲಿಗೆ} \kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಸೀಟು} \kn{ಕಾಯ್ದಿರಿಸಿದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nānu nāḷeya railige ondu sīṭu kāydiriside.} — \textquotedblleft{}I booked a seat on tomorrow's train.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ನಾಳೆಯ}} (\emph{nāḷeya}, \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow's\textquotedblright{}); \textbf{\kn{ರೈಲಿಗೆ}} (\emph{railige}, \textquotedblleft{}for the train\textquotedblright{}); \textbf{\kn{ಕಾಯ್ದಿರಿಸಿದೆ}} is the past of \textbf{\kn{ಕಾಯ್ದಿರಿಸು}}, \textquotedblleft{}to book\textquotedblright{}.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: when it leaves}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಸ್} \kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಗಂಟೆಗೆ} \kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bas eṣṭu gaṇṭege horaḍuttade?} — \textquotedblleft{}At what time does the bus leave?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಗಂಟೆಗೆ}}, \textquotedblleft{}at how many hours\textquotedblright{}, is \textquotedblleft{}at what time\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}} is \textquotedblleft{}it sets out\textquotedblright{}. The answer keeps the same shape:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಆರು} \kn{ಗಂಟೆಗೆ} \kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āru gaṇṭege horaḍuttade.} — \textquotedblleft{}It leaves at six.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

For the arrival, \textbf{\kn{ಬರುತ್ತದೆ}}, \textquotedblleft{}it comes\textquotedblright{}, takes the place of \textbf{\kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}One ticket to Mysuru, please\textquotedblright{} — \emph{maisūrige ondu ṭikeṭ koḍi}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}How much is it?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{eṣṭu āyitu?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}At what time does the bus leave?\textquotedblright{} — \emph{bas eṣṭu gaṇṭege horaḍuttade?}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I booked a seat on tomorrow's train\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nānu nāḷeya railige ondu sīṭu kāydiriside}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}One ticket, please\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}How much is it?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಆಯಿತು}?}) \textquotedblleft{}At what time does it leave?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಗಂಟೆಗೆ} \kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}?})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಔಷಧ} (auṣadha)}{ಔಷಧ (auṣadha)}]{\kn{ಔಷಧ} (auṣadha) — a medicine; a remedy}

\label{lesson:KA-C314-ausadha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say \textquotedblleft{}a fever\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}a tablet\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}a hospital\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{jvara}, \emph{mātre}, \emph{āspatre}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}At what time does the bus leave?\textquotedblright{} (\emph{bas eṣṭu gaṇṭege horaḍuttade?})
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಔಷಧ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} — \emph{auṣadha} — \textquotedblleft{}a medicine; a remedy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರಯಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಜ್ವರ} \kn{ಬಂತು}. \kn{ವೈದ್ಯರು} \kn{ಔಷಧ} \kn{ಕೊಟ್ಟರು}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{prayāṇadalli nanage jvara bantu. vaidyaru auṣadha koṭṭaru.} — \textquotedblleft{}On the journey I got a fever. The doctor gave (me) medicine.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರಯಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ}} (\emph{prayāṇadalli}, \textquotedblleft{}on the journey\textquotedblright{}). A fever \textquotedblleft{}came\textquotedblright{} to me: \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಜ್ವರ} \kn{ಬಂತು}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಈ} \kn{ಔಷಧ} \kn{ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ಎರಡು} \kn{ಸಲ} \kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ī auṣadha dinakke eraḍu sala tegedukoḷḷi.} — \textquotedblleft{}Take this medicine twice a day.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ}} (\emph{dinakke}, \textquotedblleft{}a day, per day\textquotedblright{}); \textbf{\kn{ಎರಡು} \kn{ಸಲ}}, \textquotedblleft{}two times\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\kn{ಸಲ}} of \textbf{\kn{ಇನ್ನೊಂದು} \kn{ಸಲ} \kn{ಹೇಳಿ}}; \textbf{\kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ}} is the polite \textquotedblleft{}take\textquotedblright{}.

In talk you will often hear \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧಿ}}, with a final \textbf{-\kn{ಇ}}: the same word. \textbf{\kn{ಮಾತ್ರೆ}} is one tablet; \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} is any medicine.

Its first letter is one you have not written: the vowel \emph{au}, standing at the start of a word. The next lesson takes it out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} (\emph{auṣadha}) is Sanskrit \emph{auṣadha}. CDIAL 2571 gives it as \textquotedblleft{}consisting of herbs\textquotedblright{} and, as a noun, \textquotedblleft{}herbs in general, a herb\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{ōṣadhi}, \textquotedblleft{}a herb, a plant\textquotedblright{}. Pali already has \emph{ōsadha} for \textquotedblleft{}medicine\textquotedblright{}. A word for herbs became the word for the remedy made from them.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{auṣadha}, slowly, then at speed
  \item \textquotedblleft{}On the journey I got a fever. The doctor gave me medicine.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{prayāṇadalli nanage jvara bantu. vaidyaru auṣadha koṭṭaru.}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Take this medicine twice a day\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ī auṣadha dinakke eraḍu sala tegedukoḷḷi}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} mean? (\textbf{A medicine; a remedy.}) How is it said in quick talk? (\textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧಿ}}.) What did the Sanskrit word first mean? (\textbf{Made of herbs; a herb.})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಔ} (au)}{ಔ (au)}]{\kn{ಔ} (au) — the letter that opens \kn{ಔಷಧ}}

\label{lesson:KA-S175-letter-au}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: which letters are \textbf{\kn{ಒ}} and \textbf{\kn{ಓ}}? (\emph{o} and \emph{ō}.) Which sign says \emph{au} after a consonant? (\textbf{\kn{◌ೌ}}, the mark in \textbf{\kn{ಹೌದು}}.)

Now say \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} (\emph{auṣadha}), \textquotedblleft{}a medicine\textquotedblright{}. You met it a moment ago. This lesson takes its first letter out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \kn{ಔ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಔ}} — \emph{au}.

It is an \textbf{independent vowel}: the shape \emph{au} takes at the start of a word. It is one vowel that glides from \emph{a} toward \emph{u}, the way the middle of English \emph{now} does.

After a consonant, \emph{au} is the sign \textbf{\kn{◌ೌ}}: \textbf{\kn{ಹೌದು}}, \emph{haudu}, \textquotedblleft{}yes\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\kn{ಗೌರವ}}, \emph{gaurava}, \textquotedblleft{}respect\textquotedblright{}. At the start of a word there is no consonant to carry a sign, so the vowel stands as a letter of its own. With it, every vowel this book uses has its letter for the front of a word, and all but \textbf{\kn{ಅ}} have a sign for inside one.

In print the lower part of \textbf{\kn{ಔ}} is the pair of round bowls you know from the bottom of \textbf{\kn{ಒ}}. Above them a flat bar runs along the top; on the left it drops into the body, and on the right it ends in a small curl that turns inward. Few words open with \textbf{\kn{ಔ}}, and most of them come from Sanskrit.

\subsection*{Writing: \kn{ಔ} — copy the printed shape}
Put your pen beside \textbf{\kn{ಔ}} and copy the shape you can see, slowly, and larger than it is printed. Then hold your copy against the print: two round bowls below, a flat bar along the top that drops into the body on the left, and a small curl turning inward at its right end.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you where to start this character or which way to travel. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying the printed shape needs no such source, and it is how the shape becomes yours in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Find:} \kn{ಔ} at the start of \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}}
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \kn{ಔ} three times, saying \emph{au} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \kn{ಒ}, \kn{ಓ}, then \kn{ಔ}, from memory, naming each
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}}
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \kn{ಔ}? (\emph{\textbf{au}}, at the start of a word.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}}, \emph{auṣadha}, \textquotedblleft{}a medicine\textquotedblright{}.) Which sign says \emph{au} after a consonant? (\textbf{\kn{◌ೌ}}, as in \textbf{\kn{ಹೌದು}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು} (kaḷeduhōyitu)}{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು (kaḷeduhōyitu)}]{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು} (kaḷeduhōyitu) — when something goes wrong}

\label{lesson:KA-C314-kaleduhoyitu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}to get lost\textquotedblright{} (\emph{kaḷeduhōgu}) and \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{} (\emph{dūru koḍu}). Then \textquotedblleft{}a medicine\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{auṣadha}.) Which letter opens it? (\textbf{\kn{ಔ}}, \emph{au}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: the bus got away}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ಅಯ್ಯೋ}, \kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಬಸ್} \kn{ತಪ್ಪಿಹೋಯಿತು}!}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ayyō, nanna bas tappihōyitu!} — \textquotedblleft{}Oh no, I've missed my bus!\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪಿಹೋಯಿತು}} is two pieces: \textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪಿ}}, the \textbf{-\kn{ಇ}} form of the verb \textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು}}, \textquotedblleft{}to slip, to go astray\textquotedblright{}, the verb behind the noun \textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು}}, \textquotedblleft{}a mistake\textquotedblright{}; and \textbf{\kn{ಹೋಯಿತು}}, \textquotedblleft{}it went\textquotedblright{}. Word for word: \textquotedblleft{}my bus slipped away\textquotedblright{}. Kannada says the bus got away, not that you missed it.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lost, and reported}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಚೀಲ} \kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು}. \kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಚೀಲದಲ್ಲಿ} \kn{ಇತ್ತು}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanna cīla kaḷeduhōyitu. nanna phōn cīladalli ittu.} — \textquotedblleft{}My bag is lost. My phone was in the bag.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು}} is the \textquotedblleft{}it\textquotedblright{} past of \textbf{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಗು}}; \textbf{\kn{ಇತ್ತು}} says where the phone was. \textbf{\kn{ಚೀಲದಲ್ಲಿ}} (\emph{cīladalli}, \textquotedblleft{}in the bag\textquotedblright{}). Then the report:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ಪೊಲೀಸರಿಗೆ} \kn{ದೂರು} \kn{ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nānu polīsarige dūru koṭṭe.} — \textquotedblleft{}I made a complaint to the police.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಪೊಲೀಸರಿಗೆ}} (\emph{polīsarige}, \textquotedblleft{}to the police\textquotedblright{}): \textbf{\kn{ಪೊಲೀಸ್}} with the respectful \textbf{-\kn{ರು}} and the \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} ending.

And when the trouble is your health:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ}. \kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಔಷಧ} \kn{ಬೇಕು}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanage huṣārilla. nanage auṣadha bēku.} — \textquotedblleft{}I'm not well. I need medicine.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\kn{ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ}} is \textbf{\kn{ಹುಷಾರು}}, \textquotedblleft{}careful, well\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ಇಲ್ಲ}}: \textquotedblleft{}(I am) not well\textquotedblright{}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Oh no, I've missed my bus!\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ayyō, nanna bas tappihōyitu!}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}My bag is lost. My phone was in the bag.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nanna cīla kaḷeduhōyitu. nanna phōn cīladalli ittu.}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I made a complaint to the police\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nānu polīsarige dūru koṭṭe}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I'm not well. I need medicine.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nanage huṣārilla. nanage auṣadha bēku.}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I missed my bus\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಬಸ್} \kn{ತಪ್ಪಿಹೋಯಿತು}}.) \textquotedblleft{}It got lost\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I made a complaint\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ದೂರು} \kn{ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I'm not well\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — at the station}

\label{lesson:KA-R314-at-the-station}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}a medicine\textquotedblright{} (\emph{auṣadha}) and \textquotedblleft{}clean\textquotedblright{} (\emph{svaccha}). Which letter opens the first? (\textbf{\kn{ಔ}}.) Which sits small inside the second? (\textbf{\kn{ಛ}}.)

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\kn{ಔ}} and \textbf{\kn{ಛ}}, once each from memory
\end{itemize}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} One ticket to my home town, please. At what time does the bus leave?
  \item \emph{Say it:} Is this seat free? I would like a seat by the window.
  \item \emph{Say it:} Oh no, the bus has gone. Where is the station? Is it next to the hotel?
  \item \emph{Say it:} Because I had a fever, I took medicine.
  \item \emph{Say it:} My bag is lost. My phone was in the bag.
  \item \emph{Say it:} I'm not well. I need medicine.
  \item \emph{Write it:} \textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}} and \textbf{\kn{ಸೀಟು}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}A seat\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಸೀಟು}}.) \textquotedblleft{}One ticket, please\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}At what time does it leave?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು} \kn{ಗಂಟೆಗೆ} \kn{ಹೊರಡುತ್ತದೆ}?}) \textquotedblleft{}It got lost\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಕಳೆದುಹೋಯಿತು}}.) \textquotedblleft{}A medicine\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\kn{ಔಷಧ}}, which opens with \textbf{\kn{ಔ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
